target.title: fix(msteams): proactive sends fail after conversation migration
target.body:
Closes #94939.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Microsoft Teams users could lose proactive Bot Framework sends after 6.x state migration when a non-empty legacy `msteams-conversations.json` source produced no conversation references visible in shared plugin state.

When that happens, archiving the legacy source silently removes recoverable Teams conversation data. The bot then cannot send proactively to those conversations until it receives a new message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The migration now treats a non-empty legacy Teams conversation source with zero visible migrated rows as unsafe to archive. It leaves the legacy source in place and reports a warning/change result instead of silently discarding recoverable conversation references.

The change is intentionally narrow: empty legacy sources and successfully verified migrations keep the existing archive behavior. This does not attempt to reinterpret every possible legacy migration failure.

## User Impact

Teams users and operators keep a recoverable legacy conversation reference source when migration cannot verify that references landed in shared plugin state. That reduces the risk of proactive Teams sends breaking after state migration and gives operators a clear warning instead of silent data loss.

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: recovery happens through the retried `create()` path only. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the exact crashed-create signature (live worktree at the derived path on exactly `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>`, no registry row) instead of dead-ending: it atomically claims the path in the registry (`insertRegistryWorktreeIfPathFree()`, a single Kysely `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (live row at path)` — no schema change), then re-provisions (`copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()`), preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` and recording the real resolved base. Only the claim holder may provision or destroy the path: a losing adopter provably touches nothing, and a holder whose re-provisioning fails removes the worktree and deletes its own row. The registry carries a persisted readiness contract: `readiness ('provisioning'|'ready')` (closed union; additive `ensureColumn` migration per repo precedent — backfill-as-ready is provably safe because no release tag contains the worktrees feature, and unreleased-main builds inserted rows only post-provisioning). The claim inserts `provisioning`; a single UPDATE flips to `ready` only after copy+setup succeed. Every usable-record path is gated on ready (`findLiveByOwner` filters in SQL; the entry shortcut and claim-loser throw a closed `WorktreeProvisioningError`; `restore()` revives as ready; provisioning rows are leases with heartbeats (`lastActiveAt` bumped at claim, post-copy, and at the ready flip): gc reaps only leases SILENT past `PROVISIONING_STALE_MS` — a persisted holder-liveness signal, so claim age alone can never kill a live-but-slow holder — restoring background recovery for auto-named orphans, while a reaped-mid-flight create fails closed with `WorktreeProvisioningReapedError`; a provisioning row whose directory vanished is hard-deleted (branch + row; no snapshot, no user work) so the name stays genuinely retriable). The gateway protocol's `WorktreeRecordSchema` gains an additive optional `readiness` enum (no version bump). Normal (non-adopting) `create()` uses the identical claim-early ordering (claim immediately after `git worktree add`; both paths share one claim → provision-as-holder → holder-only-cleanup helper), establishing the invariant that an in-flight create always holds a live row — so the no-row+live-worktree signature genuinely means a crashed create, and an in-flight worktree can never be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name call. Every new live registry row is uniqueness-enforced through the one claim. `reconcileOrphans()`/gc remains preserve-only (upstream behavior) — background adoption is deliberately not shipped (see Risks). `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field for the adoption signature check.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): gc keeps upstream's preserve-only behavior for foreign/detached and live git-listed worktrees (only dead debris and stale provisioning rows are cleaned); no protocol version bump; no changes to snapshot semantics; web UI status label deliberately unchanged (would pull in i18n regeneration disproportionate to this PR).

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `create()` performs the irreversible git-side effects (`git worktree add`, branch creation) before the registry insert, with no crash-window reconciliation: `reconcileOrphans()` treated "git still lists this directory as a live worktree" purely as a preserve signal and never checked whether the worktree matches the managed naming scheme but lacks a registry row.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

target.body:
## Summary

- Rebases PR #94344 onto current main and resolves the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider conflicts without changing the intended SSRF contract.
- Updates the added SSRF tests to match the exported `LookupFn` overload shape.
- Updates the memory config docs to describe exact configured `baseUrl` origin trust (`scheme://host:port`) without widening trust across protocols or ports.
- Prevents configured local-service acquisition and health probes when the selected provider explicitly sets `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false`.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Operators using configured OpenAI-compatible memory embedding providers need the selected provider's private-endpoint policy to behave predictably: omitted policy preserves exact configured origin compatibility, explicit `false` fails closed, and explicit `true` allows broader private-network access.
- **Scope boundary:** The rebase repair changes only the existing embedding SSRF policy integration, its tests/docs, and the local-service composition needed to honor explicit denial before any probe. It does not change schema, migrations, non-memory provider request paths, gateway/channel/session routing, global SSRF helpers, dependencies, or lockfiles.

Fixes #94166

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — existing PR author repair for #94344.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #94180 (`feat(memory-core): allow private network endpoints for memory embeddings`) and adjacent #96074 (`fix(memory): honor provider request proxy for embeddings`). The public-contract helper also flagged #92307 through an environment/version term, but #92307 is about exec-approval startup warnings and is not the same embedding/private-network contract.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #94180 adds a memory-specific config surface, `memorySearch.remote.network.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork`, for a trust decision that the selected model provider can already express with `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork`.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** This PR reuses the existing provider transport-trust contract as the canonical source of truth for configured providers instead of introducing a second memory-only knob. This update only repairs the review findings on that existing approach.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The current-head bounded proof exercises the real `memory status --deep --json` CLI path against a loopback/private OpenAI-compatible daemon backed by the actual FastEmbed `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` model. Omitted policy succeeds through exact-origin trust with one `/v1/embeddings` request, explicit `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false` is blocked before the daemon receives any request, and explicit `true` succeeds with one `/v1/embeddings` request.
- **Related open PR scan:** #94180 is the linked alternative for memory private endpoint support. #96074 is adjacent but distinct: it propagates the selected provider's proxy dispatcher into memory embedding HTTP transport, while this PR is limited to the provider's three-state private-network policy and deliberately does not pass proxy/auth/TLS fields into the policy resolver. #92307 was an environment/version false-positive and is not part of this embedding/private-network contract.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `openclaw memory status --deep` against a configured OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint on a loopback/private address must preserve exact-origin compatibility when provider private-network policy is omitted, must block when the selected provider explicitly sets `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false`, and must honor `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` for explicit broader private-network trust.
- **Canonical reachability path:** User `models.providers.<id>` and `agents.defaults.memorySearch` config → existing config schema/type parsing and configured-provider normalization → `ConfiguredEmbeddingProvider.request.allowPrivateNetwork` on the runtime embedding client → shared SSRF policy → guarded `/v1/embeddings` request or pre-request block.

- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused the repository shared `resolveProviderTransportSsrFPolicy` policy builder and `resolvePinnedHostnameWithPolicy` test seam. This preserves the canonical exact-origin and metadata-hostname exclusions instead of rebuilding them in the embedding adapter. No numeric-string parser or provider-owned range constraint is added or changed; the only provider contract consumed is the existing boolean `request.allowPrivateNetwork` setting.

| RF-003 | Disclosed/maintainer decision | The omitted/false/true SSRF contract remains a maintainer/security-boundary decision. This contributor update implements and proves the requested behavior but does not present that policy choice as independently approved. |
| RF-004 | Fixed within scope / disclosed | Fresh isolated configs were exercised for omitted, explicit false, and explicit true. The resolver receives only `{ allowPrivateNetwork }`; unrelated configured auth, proxy, and TLS fields are deliberately excluded, so existing embedding base URL, header, API-key, proxy, and TLS construction is unchanged. | RF-005 | Fixed/proven | Replaced the adapter-local private-network decision with `resolveProviderRequestPolicyConfig`, narrowed the resolver request input to `allowPrivateNetwork` only, and repeated the full three-state CLI proof against the real FastEmbed daemon. |
| RF-006 | Fixed/proven | The embedding client now calls the canonical provider request resolver with provider id, API, normalized base URL, `capability: "other"`, `transport: "http"`, and an `allowPrivateNetwork`-only request object. A failing-first integration test includes unrelated auth, proxy, and TLS fields and proves they are not forwarded. |
| RF-007 | Fixed/proven | Final targeted runs passed: the embedding provider suite reports 40/40 tests, provider request config reports 30/30, and canonical provider transport reports 188/188 across two files. |

- **Target test file:** `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`
- **Target files:** `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`; `docs/reference/memory-config.md`

Different ports, protocols, redirect origins, and a `memorySearch.remote.baseUrl` override on another origin remain blocked without explicit broader opt-in; metadata-like configured hostnames also do not receive implicit exact-origin trust.

```sh
pnpm exec tsc --ignoreConfig --strict --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --target ES2022 --types node --noEmit /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-94344-evidence/lookupfn-overload-smoke.ts
```

- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The rebase keeps the existing provider-policy helper and adds one composition guard so explicit denial is enforced before local-service acquisition. The owning provider test locks the combined path without expanding unrelated provider or gateway coverage.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** security-boundary, compatibility, auth-provider.
- **Risk explanation:** The PR touches the security boundary for private-network embedding fetches and the provider/config contract that decides when exact-origin or broader private-network trust is allowed. A wrong change could relax SSRF blocking by default, carry trust across ports/protocols/redirects, break existing configured local/private aliases, or create a second incompatible memory-only trust surface.
- **Why acceptable:** The PR's runtime behavior remains constrained to the canonical provider policy: omitted config preserves only the exact configured origin, explicit false denies that exact-origin trust and also prevents local-service probes, and explicit true is required for broader private-network access.
- **What did NOT change:** No schema, migration, new config key, provider parser/range, global SSRF helper, non-memory provider transport, gateway/channel/session routing, dependency, lockfile, or unrelated cleanup changed. - **Root cause:** The original issue is that memory-core OpenAI-compatible embeddings did not consistently consume the selected configured provider's `request.allowPrivateNetwork` policy when building the embedding SSRF policy. During rebase, current main's configured local-service acquisition path composed ahead of guarded fetch, so explicit denial could still trigger a private health probe before the embedding POST was blocked. The adapter also continued reading the boolean directly after current main introduced the canonical provider request resolver, creating a second policy decision path.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The embedding client now obtains `allowPrivateNetwork` and `privateNetworkExplicitlyDenied` from `resolveProviderRequestPolicyConfig`, passes only the policy field it consumes, and uses that result for both canonical provider-transport SSRF policy and local-service acquisition. Omitted trust is sourced from the selected provider's configured origin when present, so a different `memorySearch.remote.baseUrl` cannot inherit it; remote-only configurations retain their own exact-origin compatibility. Existing header/auth/proxy/TLS construction is unchanged. The fix does not add downstream fetch fallbacks, a parallel memory-only knob, or unrelated runtime changes.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix with focused author repair.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical contract surface is `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork` for configured provider transport trust. Memory embedding SSRF policy consumes that provider-owned request setting; this PR does not add a parallel `memorySearch` private-network knob, does not change schema/default values, and does not alter unrelated provider, gateway, channel, or session contracts.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** Medium-high — local CLI proof exists for the runtime path, the current author repair passes focused and full test-type verification, and the remaining SSRF/private-network acceptance is disclosed as maintainer/security judgment rather than presented as already externally approved.
- **Patch quality notes:** The `as unknown as LookupFn` casts are test-only fixtures for the overloaded `dns.promises.lookup` signature and match the existing SSRF pinning test pattern; the `EmbeddingProviderCreateOptions["config"]` casts are partial canonical config fixtures, not production type suppression. The runtime `return undefined` for explicit false is the intentional provider-denial path, and the local-service guard prevents any pre-guard probe under that same canonical config. No skipped tests, `.only`, lint disables, runtime catch-all fallback, schema migration, or new public config knob were added.

## What Problem This Solves

`normalizePollInput()` has two identical validation blocks for `durationSeconds` and `durationHours` — each parses a raw value, floors it to an integer, and throws if it's less than 1. Extracting a `normalizePositiveDuration()` helper eliminates the duplication without changing behavior.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Identical validation logic duplicated for `durationSeconds` and `durationHours` — behavior-preserving refactor
- **Real environment tested**: Node 22.22, Linux x86_64, local dev checkout (branch `refactor/polls-duration-helper-v2`)
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e "
  import { normalizePollInput } from './src/polls.js';
  console.log(JSON.stringify(normalizePollInput({ question:'Best?', options:['A','B'], durationSeconds: 3600 })));
  console.log(JSON.stringify(normalizePollInput({ question:'Best?', options:['A','B'], durationHours: 2 })));
  console.log(JSON.stringify(normalizePollInput({ question:'Best?', options:['A','B'] })));
  try { normalizePollInput({ question:'Test?', options:['a','b'], durationSeconds: 0 }); } catch(e) { console.log(e.message); }
  try { normalizePollInput({ question:'Test?', options:['a','b'], durationHours: 0 }); } catch(e) { console.log(e.message); }
  try { normalizePollInput({ question:'Test?', options:['a','b'], durationSeconds: 30, durationHours: 1 }); } catch(e) { console.log(e.message); }
  "
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```text
  $ node --import tsx -e "..."

  --- Valid poll with durationSeconds ---
  {"question":"Best framework?","options":["React","Vue"],"maxSelections":1,"durationSeconds":3600}

  --- Valid poll with durationHours ---
  {"question":"Best framework?","options":["React","Vue"],"maxSelections":1,"durationHours":2}

  --- Valid poll with no duration ---
  {"question":"Best framework?","options":["React","Vue"],"maxSelections":1}

  --- Invalid: durationSeconds = 0 ---
  durationSeconds must be at least 1

  --- Invalid: durationHours = 0 ---
  durationHours must be at least 1

  --- Invalid: both set ---
  durationSeconds and durationHours are mutually exclusive
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: All valid inputs produce identical normalized output. All invalid inputs produce identical error messages. Diff is -7 lines of duplication.
- **What was not tested**: Live poll creation through a channel plugin (e.g. Telegram, Discord)

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/polls.ts` | Added `normalizePositiveDuration()` helper; replaced two duplicated validation blocks |

target.body:
Related: #51620

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose inbound message was accepted shortly before a SIGUSR1 or config reload could have buffered message content silently dropped before it reached the reply pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway now closes ordinary work admission synchronously, flushes accepted inbound debounce work inside one core-private restart continuation, drains channel, active-turn, and followup work in order, then rechecks work created by followup delivery. Pre-created debounce callbacks reserve tracked required-continuation ownership, including parentless accepted work. Already-reserved required continuations may finish during the signal-pending gap while ordinary roots remain fenced, and removed-but-unsettled timer flushes remain visible until settlement. Buffered callbacks can also be explicitly rebound to the private restart admission context, while the global sweep is bounded by both the remaining restart deadline and a 100-pass/30-second ceiling so continued ingress cannot stall reload indefinitely.

Forced restarts retain the existing skip-drain behavior. This does not persist messages sent while the gateway is offline.

## User Impact

Messages accepted immediately before an in-process reload can complete through the normal command/reply path instead of being rejected by the restart fence or disappearing from in-memory buffers. A sustained stream of new transport events also cannot hold the gateway forever in the debounce-flush phase.

## Evidence

Exact-head validation for `38befdcf347331814f3453093ff3ef0c31cc33c0`:

- **Focused behavior tests:** 4 files, 166 tests passed.
  - `src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`: 65 passed.
  - `src/process/command-queue.test.ts`: 42 passed.
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts`: 16 passed.
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts`: 43 passed.
- **New P1 regressions:** a buffer created inside an admitted inbound root survives that root's release; timer-started required work can finish through the restart-signal-pending fence while ordinary roots remain blocked; a timer-started callback remains visible and keeps the restart sweep pending until its real command enqueue settles; parentless accepted continuations retain required ownership; continuous ingress stops at the pass cap; the exact final-pass boundary reports drained correctly; a slow callback returns at the supplied deadline.
- **Formatting/lint:** `oxfmt --check` and type-aware `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` passed on all touched files.
- **Type safety:** core production, core test, and plugin SDK declaration `tsgo` checks passed.
- **Tree identity:** GitHub tree `0e31967c65a163de007374e202e0eabb87e95337` is the exact locally tested tree; all five uploaded blob SHAs matched the local Git objects.
- **CI:** GitHub Actions is running on the exact head above.

A live Signal/Telegram account is not paired in this environment. I have requested the repository's Mantis Telegram proof flow below so maintainers can attach redacted channel-to-gateway reload evidence to this exact head.

## Implementation and Safety Notes

- `createInboundDebouncer()` retains its public `enqueue` / `flushKey` / `cancelKey` return shape.
- `ChannelRunQueue` retains its public `enqueue` / `deactivate` shape.
- No public `enqueueInternal`, `allowDuringGatewayDrain`, or command-queue admission bypass is exposed.

- The branch remains a focused 13-file change.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: recovery happens through the retried `create()` path only. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the exact crashed-create signature (live worktree at the derived path on exactly `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>`, no registry row) instead of dead-ending: it atomically claims the path in the registry (`insertRegistryWorktreeIfPathFree()`, a single Kysely `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (live row at path)` — no schema change), then re-provisions (`copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()`), preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` and recording the real resolved base. Only the claim holder may provision or destroy the path: a losing adopter provably touches nothing, and a holder whose re-provisioning fails removes the worktree and deletes its own row. The registry carries a persisted readiness contract: `readiness ('provisioning'|'ready')` (closed union; additive `ensureColumn` migration per repo precedent — backfill-as-ready is provably safe because no release tag contains the worktrees feature, and unreleased-main builds inserted rows only post-provisioning). The claim inserts `provisioning`; a single UPDATE flips to `ready` only after copy+setup succeed. Every usable-record path is gated on ready (`findLiveByOwner` filters in SQL; the entry shortcut and claim-loser throw a closed `WorktreeProvisioningError`; `restore()` revives as ready; provisioning rows are leases with heartbeats (`lastActiveAt` bumped at claim, post-copy, and at the ready flip): gc reaps only leases SILENT past `PROVISIONING_STALE_MS` — a persisted holder-liveness signal, so claim age alone can never kill a live-but-slow holder — restoring background recovery for auto-named orphans, while a reaped-mid-flight create fails closed with `WorktreeProvisioningReapedError`; a provisioning row whose directory vanished is hard-deleted (branch + row; no snapshot, no user work) so the name stays genuinely retriable). The gateway protocol's `WorktreeRecordSchema` gains an additive optional `readiness` enum (no version bump). Normal (non-adopting) `create()` uses the identical claim-early ordering (claim immediately after `git worktree add`; both paths share one claim → provision-as-holder → holder-only-cleanup helper), establishing the invariant that an in-flight create always holds a live row — so the no-row+live-worktree signature genuinely means a crashed create, and an in-flight worktree can never be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name call. Every new live registry row is uniqueness-enforced through the one claim. `reconcileOrphans()`/gc remains preserve-only (upstream behavior) — background adoption is deliberately not shipped (see Risks). `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field for the adoption signature check.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): gc keeps upstream's preserve-only behavior for foreign/detached and live git-listed worktrees (only dead debris and stale provisioning rows are cleaned); no protocol version bump; no changes to snapshot semantics; web UI status label deliberately unchanged (would pull in i18n regeneration disproportionate to this PR).

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #103239
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `create()` performs the irreversible git-side effects (`git worktree add`, branch creation) before the registry insert, with no crash-window reconciliation: `reconcileOrphans()` treated "git still lists this directory as a live worktree" purely as a preserve signal and never checked whether the worktree matches the managed naming scheme but lacks a registry row.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no adopt-or-repair path for the crashed-create signature; `create()`'s branch-exists guard had no way to distinguish "user's foreign branch" from "our own crashed create()".
- Contributing context (if known): the registry has no `name` column (name derives from the path's last segment), so adoption needs no extra bookkeeping — the orphan is fully re-derivable from path + branch.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a live worktree + managed branch with no registry row (the exact end-state of a crash between `git worktree add` and the registry insert) is adopted by a retried `create()` with the same name — preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId`, re-running provisioning (include files + setup script restored, real `baseRef` recorded), and holding the loser-touches-nothing / holder-only-destruction invariants under deterministic interleavings; gc during an in-flight normal `create()` adopts nothing and exactly one live row remains; a parked in-flight create cannot be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name retry (same-owner and foreign-owner both covered, setup executes exactly once); a failing setup leaves no worktree, branch, or registry row.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests use the real `git` binary and real SQLite registry (the file's established pattern — no mocks), produce the crash end-state via production code (`create()` then deleting only the registry row), and assert through the public service API only.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): "deletes unregistered orphan debris but preserves git-listed worktrees" covers the foreign/detached case and stays green, locking in that non-managed worktrees are never claimed.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — two new tests added.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- A retried `create()` with the same name after a crashed create now succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record) instead of failing with `branch already exists`.
- gc behavior is unchanged from upstream (preserve-only for live worktrees); foreign or detached-HEAD worktrees are unaffected.
- Concurrent same-path registrations can no longer produce duplicate live registry rows (atomic claim; loser gets the existing "name already in use" semantics).
- `list()` now shows a worktree from claim-time (during provisioning) rather than after setup completes; failed creates still end with no registry row.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): "branch already exists" (dead end; manual git surgery required)

After:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): exact orphan signature -> atomic path claim -> re-provision
     (owner + real base preserved) -> returns record
  -> claim loser (concurrent registration won): touches nothing; standard in-use semantics
  -> gc: preserve-only (unchanged upstream behavior)
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A. Adoption is gated on an exact `git worktree list --porcelain` path + `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>` branch match; fabricating that state requires local filesystem/git access equivalent to what `create()` already requires. `insertRegistryWorktree` is the same call path `create()` already uses.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26 (arm64); fix is platform-independent (pure git + SQLite service logic)
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / bun, source checkout
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): default `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`-backed state

### Steps

1. `ManagedWorktreeService.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` and kill the process after `git worktree add` completes but before the registry insert (repro: create normally, then delete only the registry row — identical end state).
2. Run `service.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` again.

### Expected

- retried create succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record); gc preserves the orphan untouched.

### Actual

- Before this PR: gc skips it forever; retried create throws `branch already exists: openclaw/task-1`. After this PR: expected behavior (see tests).

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Before (tests added, fix stashed):

```
❯ |agents| src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts (24 tests | 2 failed)
FAIL … adopts a worktree orphaned when create() crashed …, during gc()
  AssertionError: expected undefined to match object {…}
FAIL … adopts an orphaned worktree instead of throwing on a retried create() …
  Error: branch already exists: openclaw/orphan-retry
```

After:

```
pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  41 passed (41) agents shard + 23 passed state shard
```

Real-behavior proof on the FROZEN FINAL head e5b7677497 (all four requested scenarios — active holder survives gc, SIGKILLed holder reaped after lease expiry and recreated fully provisioned, missing-path claim cleaned to a retriable name, pre-column DB backfills ready): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4947439791. Earlier ordering-specific transcript: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103390#issuecomment-4944938951 — Window B is a genuine mid-provisioning SIGKILL (exit 137) showing the crash state is observable (claim-time row, missing setup marker), gc preserves it, and the operator recovery path works end-to-end (remove() cleans worktree+branch, fresh create fully provisions); Window A (add→claim, no user code) is a labeled constructed end-state recovered by retried-create adoption with full re-provisioning. Supersedes the earlier transcript (#issuecomment-4937129438), which demonstrated the pre-claim-early ordering.

Also green on the touched surface: `pnpm tsgo:core` (exit 0), `oxlint` (0 findings), `oxfmt --check` (formatted). Note: repo-wide `pnpm check` currently fails in its preflight `npm shrinkwrap guard` on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout in this environment (`ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` for the `defu` override) — pre-existing and unrelated; no lockfile/override files are touched by this PR.

The previously-acknowledged gc-vs-create double-insert race is now eliminated by the atomic path claim (deterministic interleaving tests cover both directions, with a pasted negative control showing the pre-claim code produces the duplicate row). Remaining narrow edge deliberately out of scope: a lingering *removed* registry row at the same path still blocks create()-side adoption for a fresh orphan (name-reuse-after-remove + crash sequence).

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: full scoped test suite (25/25) against real git + real SQLite locally, including both new adoption tests and the pre-existing foreign-worktree preservation test; typecheck/lint/format on the touched files.
- Edge cases checked: detached-HEAD foreign worktree (preserved), bare branch collision without a live worktree (still throws), owner preservation (`workboard`/`ownerId`) on retried-create adoption including `findLiveByOwner()` lookup, crash-before-setup retry re-provisioning (include file + setup marker restored, real base recorded), and full cleanup on a failing setup script during adoption-retry.
- What you did **not** verify: a literal `kill -9` mid-`create()` on a production gateway (the crash end-state is reproduced through the service's own code paths instead); the two out-of-scope narrow edges above.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: schema/migration surface (new `readiness` column).
  - Mitigation: additive `ensureColumn` per the repo's established migration pattern; backfill default provably correct (see body); legacy-DB backfill test included; fresh-vs-migrated CHECK divergence is unobservable to prod writes (closed TS union at every write site).
- Risk: adopting a worktree that a user intentionally created outside the managed API at the exact managed path on an `openclaw/<name>` branch.
  - Mitigation: that state is indistinguishable from (and equivalent to) a crashed managed create; adoption only registers it — it never deletes or modifies the worktree.
- Risk: concurrent adoption attempts (gc vs retried create) racing for one path.
  - Mitigation: eliminated — adoption is a single-statement atomic path claim with explicit loser handling; losers never provision, mutate, or destroy; covered by deterministic interleaving tests in both directions.

target.title: fix(signal): include quoted reply context for agents
target.body:
Closes #98287
Related: #98234 (non-duplicate reply-session initialization conflict/drop issue)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal users sending quoted replies could have the quoted target extracted into `ReplyToBody` metadata while the agent-facing `BodyForAgent` remained only the new ambiguous message, such as `Did this get done?`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inbound handling now renders visible quoted-reply context directly into `BodyForAgent` as a clear blockquote while preserving clean `RawBody`, `CommandBody`, and `BodyForCommands` for command parsing and hooks. The shared inbound metadata renderer skips only the duplicate one-hop reply-target block when the Signal-generated wrapper exactly matches the expected quoted body and sender; richer `ReplyChain` context and ordinary user-authored blockquotes still render normally.

## User Impact

Signal quoted replies now carry the referenced message into agent-facing input, so agents can answer ambiguous followups using the intended quoted target. Plain non-quoted Signal messages remain unchanged, and quoted context is not duplicated in the model prompt when Signal has already inlined the generated quote block.

## Evidence

Duplicate search before filing found no open narrow issue/PR for `Signal quoted reply BodyForAgent` / `agent-facing body`; the closest existing items were closed #68665 and related-but-different #84364, plus broad open quote-reply PRs that do not provide this narrow BodyForAgent fix.

Validation run locally:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts extensions/signal/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo && node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src` (29 files, 375 tests)
- `git diff --check`
- Exact-head regression coverage now canonicalizes blank lines in multi-paragraph quoted text (`>` with no trailing space) and proves the duplicate metadata block stays suppressed.
- Debounced Signal batches now render reply context per entry before joining the batch, with quoted-first/plain-last and plain-first/quoted-last regressions and an internal exact-once marker that preserves the last structured reply metadata without duplicating it in the prompt.
- Fresh GitHub CI is running after the only preceding failure—two formatter-only line wraps in the Signal handler—was fixed on exact head `8087d6f852d51bf20dd0bca1d13c900219d6e3ed`, which includes the shared upstream cutoff `262baedcf7fa3d66dc35cce7d0253e0a31f0cc0e`.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --prompt 'Review the final Signal quoted-reply BodyForAgent change after exact generated-prefix duplicate checks that include expected sender and boundary. Confirm no accepted duplicate-context, equal-body, spoofed marker/altered wrapper, ReplyChain, or command/raw body regressions remain.'` clean with no accepted/actionable findings.

Caveat: no live Signal device roundtrip was run in this isolated checkout. The proof is source-level focused tests, the full Signal plugin Vitest directory, TypeScript checks, format/whitespace checks, and autoreview.

AI-assisted implementation; no agent transcript is included because this task involved private Signal context and the local transcript prompt flow was unavailable in this run mode.

target.body:
Closes #104524

AI-assisted: yes. I used an OpenAI coding agent, reviewed the resulting change, and understand the timeout behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users could have all outbound replies for a session stall for roughly eight minutes when an API call used a method that was not explicitly listed in the client timeout table.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every identified Telegram API method except `getUpdates` now receives the existing 60-second outbound timeout as a default. Explicit method-specific guards remain unchanged, higher configured timeouts are still honored, and requests whose method cannot be identified remain untouched.

## User Impact

A newly introduced or otherwise unlisted Telegram API method can no longer silently fall back to grammY's approximately 500-second timeout and park the serialized delivery lane. Its client-side guard defaults to 60 seconds unless the operator configured a higher timeout.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — 1 file, 15 tests passed.
- `pnpm test:extension telegram` — 142 files, 2,666 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.ts extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.ts extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — formatting passed.
- `NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=2300' node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/telegram/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

No live Telegram probe was run because this checkout has no test-bot credentials. The linked issue includes the production incident evidence and reports the same fallback behavior running in production.

### Controlled runtime proof

A credential-free controlled Bot API endpoint exercised the real `createTelegramClientFetch` and `AbortController` path on this PR branch. All three requests ran concurrently against delayed local HTTP responses; no Telegram token or external API was used.

```text
controlled_endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>/bot<redacted>/METHOD
unlisted-default: answerCallbackQuery, server delay 65000ms -> aborted after 60004ms: Telegram answercallbackquery timed out after 60000ms
unlisted-configured-override: answerCallbackQuery, configured timeout 70s, server delay 62000ms -> HTTP 200 after 62030ms
getUpdates-unchanged: getUpdates, configured timeout 70s, server delay 65000ms -> aborted after 45015ms: Telegram getupdates timed out after 45000ms
proof_result=PASS
```

This demonstrates the 60-second fallback through the actual fetch wrapper, the existing higher configured-timeout escape hatch, and the unchanged 45-second `getUpdates` guard.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

## Linked context

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
